# Vehicle config fields

*Source: the `*VehicleConfigDataAsset`, `MTrackedVehicleWheelData`, `BHRotaryFlightDataAsset`, `BHAirVehicleDragDataAsset` and `WDVehicleGameplayComponentsDataAsset` exports under the vehicle plugins. Generated by [`_tools/vehicle_round85_tables.py`](https://github.com/Kiyogitpy/wardogs-data-docs/blob/main/_tools/vehicle_round85_tables.py). Evidence and status: [round 85 vehicles](https://github.com/Kiyogitpy/wardogs-data-docs/blob/main/docs/evidence/round85-veh.md).*

[Vehicle parts and handling](Wardogs_VehicleHandling_v1.md) holds the engine, axle, wheel and suspension tables. This page adds the fields it leaves out. `-` means the asset does not set the field (a native default applies, see the defaults section of that page).

### Tracked wheel data (`MTrackedVehicleWheelData`)

| Asset | Suspension length | Wheel radius | Spring rate | Damping compress | Damping rebound | Max incline (deg) | Incline grip multiplier (X, Y, Z) | Lateral friction | Steering friction reduction | Unnamed float (`_aaabodchgifaioegpnmah`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`DA_SPW_01_WheelData`](https://github.com/Kiyogitpy/wardogs-data-docs/blob/main/data/Wardogs/Plugins/GameFeatures/Vehicles/SPW_01/Content/Data/DA_SPW_01_WheelData.json) | 40 | 38 | 112,500 | 12,000 | 17,000 | 50 | (1, 2, 1) | 3.5 | - | 4.5 |
| [`DA_TNK_01_WheelData`](https://github.com/Kiyogitpy/wardogs-data-docs/blob/main/data/Wardogs/Plugins/GameFeatures/Vehicles/TNK_01/Content/Data/DA_TNK_01_WheelData.json) | 40 | 35 | 112,500 | 12,000 | 17,000 | 50 | (1, 2, 1) | 3.25 | 1 | 4.5 |
| [`DA_TNK_04_WheelData`](https://github.com/Kiyogitpy/wardogs-data-docs/blob/main/data/Wardogs/Plugins/GameFeatures/Vehicles/TNK_04/Content/Data/DA_TNK_04_WheelData.json) | 40 | 40.5 | 112,500 | 12,000 | 17,000 | 50 | (1, 2, 1) | 3.335 | 0.75 | 4.5 |

The tracks share the spring rate (112,500), damping (12,000 / 17,000), suspension length (40) and 50 degree incline limit; they differ in wheel radius (SPW 38, TNK_01 35, TNK_04 40.5) and lateral friction (3.5, 3.25, 3.335). SPW_01 sets no steering friction reduction (native default).

**What the fields do.** The fuel component's tick (native `0x7666FA0`, round 85) subtracts `rate x dt + leak x dt` from the fuel attribute each frame while the owning vehicle's network role is 3 (`ROLE_Authority`: the drain runs only where the vehicle is authoritative, a host or server; round 88, static reading) and the component is not flagged off. The `rate` term is only added when the vehicle's `bIsEngineRunning` flag is set (round 88: the extra owner check of round 85 is that flag); the `leak` term does not depend on it, so a vehicle with its engine off still loses fuel to a leak. `rate` comes from `0x7665DB0`:

- Moving: `rate = speed(km/h) / 3600 / KML` litres per second, so a vehicle burns 1/KML litres per kilometre and `Max fuel x KML` kilometres is the range on a full tank (derived).
- At or below the idle speed threshold (`IdleSpeedThreshold`, never set in the cooked assets; the constructor default is **1.0 km/h**, round 88) the rate switches from speed to the engine RPM, and divides by `RPML` instead of `KML`: `rate = RPM / 3600 / RPML` litres per second (**Native**, static reading). Wheeled vehicles read the engine RPM of their movement simulation; helicopters read a rotor or engine RPM from their rotary component; tracked vehicles and the airplane return 0, so they burn nothing while stopped or crawling at 1 km/h or less. Worked example (**Derived**): a Humvee idling at its 700 RPM idle setting with `RPML` 110 burns 700 / 3600 / 110 = 0.0018 L/s, about 0.11 L per minute, against about 5.6 L per minute at 100 km/h (100 / 3600 / 0.3 = 0.093 L/s); this assumes the simulation holds the engine at its idle RPM while stopped.
- Other constructor defaults of the fuel settings (**Native**, `0x7665AC0`): `MaxFuel` 100, `KML` 1.0, `RPML` 1500, boost multiplier 1.5, and two further floats 20 and 95 that the rate does not use (one is presumably `LowFuelThreshold`). The cooked assets override `MaxFuel`, `KML` and `RPML` for most vehicles in the table above (a `-` there means the constructor default applies).
- The rate is multiplied by the boost multiplier while boosting, and by a fuel-usage multiplier from character skills (`FuelUsageReduction`, see the Driver and Pilot skill tables).
- `leak` is the stored fuel-leak value set by the fuel-tank damage effects (0.1 to 3.0 litres per second, see [Fuel and refueling](../_wiki/vehicles/fuel-and-refueling.md)).


Which settings field each native slot holds is inferred from how the value is used; the component constructor (`0x7665AC0`) confirms the order KML, idle threshold, RPML, then the boost multiplier, which differs from the SDK field order. The listed economy in the vendor stats equals 1/KML for most vehicles (Havoc 4.4, Humvee 3.3, Kodiak 2.9, Bobcat 2.2, Dune Buggy 5.0, Ural 4.0, M113 5.7, SPH-2 and L2A6 8.0, Gepard 10.0); the T-72B3 is the exception (vendor 8.5, 1/KML 6.96). The airplane sets no fuel settings at all.

`InactivityLifetimeOutSafeZone` is the only inactivity field any asset sets: Havoc 90 s, the MH-6 family 10 s, the stationary emplacements 30,000 s. The other vehicles keep the native default, which is not in the data. Reading the name, an unoccupied vehicle outside a safe zone is removed after that time (**Derived**). The client executable only copies the value into the vehicle's gameplay-systems component at start-up (offset 1884, `0x767BC40`) and has no function that reads it back, so the timer runs on the server and could not be traced; the vehicle lifetime manager (`UBHVehicleLifetimeManager`) holds separate server-side lifetime settings. Every asset that sets `InventorySettings` makes the vehicle inventory accessible; the assets without it are stationary emplacement, Bobcat, Dune Buggy, Fixed-wing airplane. The M113 APC SV also sets an unnamed float of 0.1 there. `FactionSettings` appears only on the stationary emplacements: none changes faction (`bShouldFactionChange` false), and STN_04 turns neutral after 36,000 s. Every asset sets the same lock cue tag `GameplayCue.Vehicle.LockStateChange`, so locking has no per-vehicle setting here.

**Same-faction-only occupants** (`bAllowSameFactionOccupantsOnly` true on the `WDVehicleInteractionsDataAsset`): [`DA_VehicleInteractions_ROT_02`](https://github.com/Kiyogitpy/wardogs-data-docs/blob/main/data/Wardogs/Plugins/GameFeatures/Vehicles/ROT_02/Content/Data/DA_VehicleInteractions_ROT_02.json), [`DA_VehicleInteractions_SPW`](https://github.com/Kiyogitpy/wardogs-data-docs/blob/main/data/Wardogs/Plugins/GameFeatures/Vehicles/SPW_01/Content/Data/DA_VehicleInteractions_SPW.json), [`DA_VehicleInteractions_TNK_03`](https://github.com/Kiyogitpy/wardogs-data-docs/blob/main/data/Wardogs/Plugins/GameFeatures/Vehicles/TNK_01/Content/Data/AntiAir/DA_VehicleInteractions_TNK_03.json), [`DA_VehicleInteractions_TNK_01_Artillery`](https://github.com/Kiyogitpy/wardogs-data-docs/blob/main/data/Wardogs/Plugins/GameFeatures/Vehicles/TNK_01/Content/Data/Artillery/DA_VehicleInteractions_TNK_01_Artillery.json), [`DA_VehicleInteractions_TNK_01_Heavy`](https://github.com/Kiyogitpy/wardogs-data-docs/blob/main/data/Wardogs/Plugins/GameFeatures/Vehicles/TNK_01/Content/Data/Heavy/DA_VehicleInteractions_TNK_01_Heavy.json), [`DA_VehicleInteractions_TNK_04`](https://github.com/Kiyogitpy/wardogs-data-docs/blob/main/data/Wardogs/Plugins/GameFeatures/Vehicles/TNK_04/Content/Data/DA_VehicleInteractions_TNK_04.json) (6 of 28 interaction assets). **Native** (the enter check of the vehicle operator component, `0x7693880`): with the flag set, a player may enter only when the vehicle's faction equals the player's faction or the vehicle is neutral, and every player already seated must also match the vehicle's faction; otherwise the enter is denied. Without the flag the check is skipped, and a separate rule (a vehicle state test, not decoded) still denies enemy-faction entry to a non-neutral vehicle. Every other vehicle leaves the flag unset. `MaxInteractDistanceRadius` is set on one asset only.

The fragment gives a vehicle a box that breaks destructible geometry it runs into. **Native** (the destruction-invoker component, `0x6BC96E0`, `0x6BC9160`, `0x6BC9250`, `0x6BC9450`): every physics step the component sweeps the collision box (centre and size from the table) along the vehicle's velocity, shifting the box ahead by velocity times `VelocityOffsetMultiplier` (a look-ahead in seconds: 0.2 s on helicopters, 0.25 s on tracked vehicles, 0.075 s on wheeled ones). Ramming only counts when speed times `VehicleMass` reaches a threshold held by the destruction system (its value was not read). For each destructible chunk that breaks, the vehicle is damaged by `DamageRecievedWhenChunkDestroyed` (a vehicle health damage call, once per chunk), and an amount supplied by the destruction event is added to a pending total (clamped to 0 to 300,000) that a delayed callback turns into an impulse on the vehicle against the direction of its velocity, scaled by `CounterForceMultiplier` (zero on helicopters, so they take no recoil). A `-` in the table is a field the asset does not set (the component then uses the zero default). A `-` is a field the asset does not set (a native default applies); `bPlayerCustomizable` is false on the platforms that set it.
